findings.title: #854's brief says a both-sides-commit outcome 'is a new defect for its own ticket'; no such ticket exists

findings.title: The new AC2 guard cell reds on exactly the World-contaminated rig that AC1 exists to make skip
findings.evidence: Ticket line (AC1): "On a rig database with a bootstrapped world, T10b skips with a reason naming world contamination, or the documented recipe is proven to prevent the contamination." T10b itself now does skip. But the sibling cell added for AC2 — packages/db/tests/rig-isolation.test.mjs, `test("T10b-AC2 worldSchemaPresent() reads false on a no-World rig (the skip arm cannot become universal)")` — is guarded only by `if (unready(t)) return;` and then runs `assert.equal(await worldSchemaPresent(), false, ...)`. On a database with a bootstrapped World that assertion FAILS, so rig-isolation.test.mjs goes red on the very rig configuration #866 set out to stop going red. The failure message does name the cause, so triage is quick, but the battery's behaviour on a contaminated rig is 'one red' rather than 'one named skip'.
findings.required_fix: Give that cell the same named skip arm T10b has: `if (await worldSchemaPresent()) { t.skip("World contamination (#866): ..."); return; }` before the assertion — the guard's purpose (catching a skip arm that silently became universal on a CLEAN rig) is preserved, and the contaminated rig gets the skip AC1 promises. Cheap, one hunk, no behaviour change on the lane rigs.

findings.title: #854 AC2's 'asserts exactly one' is met by neither cell
findings.evidence: Ticket line (AC2): "Each reads standing postings off committed rows and asserts exactly one." obw.race.opening_then_evidence asserts `assert.equal(standing.length, s.drafts.all.length, ...)`, and s.drafts.all.length is >= 3 by the seed's own design (obw.siblings_ok asserts `s.drafts.all.length >= 3` as mandatory setup). obw.race.evidence_then_opening asserts `s.drafts.all.length + 1`. Both DO read off committed rows via postedEntriesOnDocument (the AC's real substance), and the multi-item deviation is defensible — #821's whole carve-out is that many opening items legitimately share one tie document — but the AC's literal count is not what either cell pins, and in the second arrival order the count is the defect itself.
findings.required_fix: No code change needed for the first arrival order; record in the ticket's closing note that AC2 was reinterpreted as 'exactly the seed's own item count and nothing else' because a single-item opening seed is not a shape this battery can build, and that the second order's count is the measured defect tracked by L04B-SPEC-01.

findings.title: sharedDependents() inner-joins pg_database, so a SHARED-object dependency (dbid = 0) is invisible — and apply() would then partially drop
findings.evidence: packages/db/scripts/role-census-reset.mjs: `from pg_shdepend sd join pg_database d on d.oid = sd.dbid join pg_authid a on a.oid = sd.refobjid`. pg_shdepend records dbid = 0 for a dependency on a SHARED object (a database-level or tablespace-level ACL, or ownership of a database). The inner join drops every such row, so check() reports 'exists, no shared dependents -- safe to drop' for a role that DROP ROLE will in fact refuse. apply()'s contract — its own header says it 'REFUSES outright ... never a partial drop' — is then broken: it iterates result.minted in order, so it would drop clara_stripe_webhook and clara_stripe_webhook_login successfully and only then throw on clara_auth_wall, leaving the cluster half-reset. Latent, not live: I queried clara_l04 directly and pg_shdepend has 0 rows with dbid = 0 today (all clara% rows sit at dbid 16384, deptypes a/o/r).
findings.required_fix: Use a LEFT JOIN and coalesce the label (`coalesce(d.datname, '<shared object>')`), or count rows straight off pg_shdepend without the pg_database join, so a dbid = 0 dependency is reported and blocks apply() like any other.

findings.title: The lint only sees git-TRACKED files, so the commit that introduces a malformed fixture is the one commit it cannot catch
findings.evidence: Ticket line (AC1): "The check runs from the lint chain and exits non-zero on a seeded malformed path (self-test proves it), naming file and path." scanTargetFiles() is `execFileSync("git", ["ls-files", ...roots])`. A brand-new fixture file that has not been `git add`ed is not listed, so a local `pnpm lint` before the first add passes over it. The self-test works around this by staging a decoy (I confirmed the worktree is left clean afterwards), which is exactly the tell. Pre-commit/CI runs see the file once it is staged, so the exposure is 'the author's own pre-add lint', not CI — but AC1's promise reads as unconditional. This finding was raised in the first review as L04-S11 and was explicitly left unfixed; it does not appear in the lane's own final report.
findings.required_fix: Either add `--cached --others --exclude-standard` to the ls-files call so untracked, non-ignored files are scanned too, or state the tracked-files limitation in the script header and in packages/db/tests/README.md's #857 section so nobody reads the lint as stronger than it is.

findings.title: commitOrCapture is an unrequested behaviour change to a driver three other cells already depend on
findings.evidence: Ticket line (Key interfaces): "`humanHoldThenContend`: gains an isolation option per side." The diff adds that, and also replaces both `await c1.query("commit").catch(() => c1.query("rollback")...)` calls with commitOrCapture(), which folds a commit-time failure into out.a / out.b instead of swallowing it. It is arguably necessary — a SERIALIZABLE side can only lose at COMMIT — but it changes how a commit failure surfaces for the three pre-existing cle.race.* cells that were not part of this ticket. Regression-checked, not merely asserted: I re-ran coding-lane-evidence-link.test.mjs, 8/8 pass (ok 1..ok 8), and wave-b/wb-k-approval.test.mjs 14/14.
findings.required_fix: None — keep it, but name the driver change in #854's closing note so the next reader of cle.race.* knows the swallow is gone.

findings.title: The new #866 README section carries a broken, and dead, citation
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/README.md:126 reads `(\`pnpm --filter @clara/runtime exec bootstrap\`, [runtime README §engine-bootstrap]` and the destination `(../../runtime/README.md)` sits on the NEXT line — CommonMark allows no whitespace between the link text and the opening paren, so GitHub renders this as literal `[runtime README §engine-bootstrap] (../../runtime/README.md)`. Separately, `grep -n -i bootstrap packages/runtime/README.md` shows no heading named engine-bootstrap anywhere in that 93KB file (the command itself is real — the same invocation appears at runtime README lines 270 and 1275), so the cited section does not exist. The repo's own check-dead-citations.mjs passes, i.e. it does not police this citation shape.
findings.required_fix: Put the link back on one line and point it at a heading that exists in packages/runtime/README.md, or drop the §anchor and cite the file plus the command only.

findings.title: depLabel() models a deptype DROP ROLE never refuses on, and leaves the one that actually occurs unlabelled
findings.evidence: packages/db/scripts/role-census-reset.mjs: `const kind = row.deptype === "a" ? "privilege" : row.deptype === "o" ? "ownership" : row.deptype === "m" ? "membership" : row.deptype;`. pg_shdepend does not record role membership — that lives in pg_auth_members — so the "m" branch is unreachable, and DROP ROLE does not refuse on membership at all (which is precisely the surprise the lane's own #867 incident note records: dropping the two _login roles succeeded despite their memberships). Meanwhile deptype 'r' (RLS policy) DOES occur on this cluster — 51 rows for clara_agent_ro, 199 for clara_authenticated, 291 for clara_fn_owner, measured just now — and falls through to the bare letter.
findings.required_fix: Drop the "m" branch and label "r" as 'RLS policy'; the operator reading a BLOCKED verdict should not have to look up a catalog letter.

findings.title: The issue body asked for 'every literal or templated field_path'; only literals are checked, and the 8 templated sites are not recorded anywhere
findings.evidence: Issue body: "A small script asserting that every literal or templated `field_path` under `packages/{db,runtime}/tests` conforms to the grammar...". The newest Agent Brief narrows this to "scanning the two test trees for field-path literals", and the brief wins under WORK-ORDER rule 2, so the implementation is compliant — extractFieldPathLiterals deliberately skips backtick forms and `${...}` interpolation, and the self-test pins that as intended behaviour. But `grep -rnoE "field_path\s*:\s*\\\`" packages/db/tests packages/runtime/tests` finds 8 templated sites, and neither the script header, the README section nor the lane report says how many sites the lint is blind to.
findings.required_fix: Add the count (8 templated sites today) to packages/db/tests/README.md's #857 section so the lint's blind spot is a measured number rather than a category.

findings.title: #857's CHECK-arm residual is unfiled, and the ticket must not close on the lint alone without it
findings.evidence: Ticket line (AC2): "Under the CHECK arm: a raw insert of an unregistered-namespace path is refused with the grammar's typed code; a NULL path inserts; a forty-row trial balance at the plural literal inserts in full." The brief's 'Either or both' framing makes the CHECK optional, so 'STOPPED' is a legitimate disposition — and I confirmed on the live rig that the CHECK and the boolean sibling genuinely do not exist, so a new migration really is required and WORK-ORDER rule 5 forbids it here. But the triage comment states the structural preference plainly ("a table CHECK on a boolean sibling of the grammar function catches every raw writer structurally"), and `gh issue list --state all --search "document_regions field_path CHECK"` returns only #857 itself and the closed #778 — nothing tracks the residual.
findings.required_fix: File the residual ('document_regions.field_path CHECK constraint, #857 residual' — a new migration adding a boolean sibling of clara._assert_field_path plus a CHECK admitting NULL and leaving opening_tb.line / prior_gl.line untouched; AC2 above is its acceptance test), or leave #857 open with the lint half recorded as landed. Do not close #857 silently on the lint.

summary: Spec axis, four tickets, 12 findings: 1 blocker, 1 major, 4 minor, 6 notes. Every count the lane reports reproduced on the lane rig (36/35/1-skip across the three claim-carrying db files, 32/32 on the three regression consumers, lint exit 0 and selftest 21/21 with a clean worktree), and every 'stopped' or 'live on main' claim I could check is true — I verified #857's CHECK arm is genuinely absent from the live catalog, that main carries none of the four deliverables, that main's T17b canary does not already cover #866 AC2, that migration 0037's entry-row-lock-first claim is real, and that the cluster is clean after the lane's #866 sibling clone and its self-disclosed #867 drop/restore incident (18 clara roles, no stray schemas, no stray databases). The one blocker is not a code defect: #854's brief says in so many words that a both-sides-commit outcome 'is a new defect for its own ticket', the cells MEASURE exactly that (a real double posting on migration 0213's opening-lane evidence wall), the suite is green over it, and no issue exists — the lane and any fix round are barred from GitHub, so the integrator must file it before merge. The major is #867 AC1's unperformed run: the documented-recipe fallback IS delivered, but 'record the run' is not, so the ticket stays open. The minors worth fixing in code are small and cheap: #866's new AC2 guard cell reds on exactly the World-contaminated rig AC1 exists to make skip (give it the same named skip arm), and role-census-reset's sharedDependents() inner-joins pg_database so a shared-object dependency (dbid = 0) goes unseen, which would make apply() partially drop in breach of its own 'never a partial drop' contract (latent today — 0 such rows on this cluster).
reviewer_notes: Read-only review: no tracked file was edited, nothing was committed, no process was killed, no other worktree touched. The only writes were this report and three throwaway probe scripts in the session scratchpad.

`git diff origin/main..HEAD` (two-dot, as the task worded it) additionally shows main's own later commits as spurious deletions of docs/PROGRESS.md and three riders/refresh-wave files. I used the three-dot form the skill specifies; the lane deleted nothing.

The whole packages/db suite was never run by the lane or by me — WORK-ORDER rule 8 asks only for touched files plus operation-census and rig-isolation, which is satisfied. #857 AC3's 'the db and runtime suites are unchanged' is therefore inferred from the touched-file set, not measured.
The Standards axis runs separately and is not represented here.
